concepts.title: Variables and Data Types
concepts.description: Learn about Python variables and basic data types

teachingContent.beginner: Variables in Python don't need type declaration. Python automatically figures out the type based on the value you assign.
teachingContent.intermediate: Python is dynamically typed. Variables can change type during execution. Use type() to check types.
teachingContent.advanced: Understanding Python's type system, duck typing, and the difference between mutable and immutable types.

crossQuestions: How do you create a variable in Python?
What are the basic data types in Python?
How do you check the type of a variable?

concepts.title: Lists and List Methods
concepts.description: Work with Python lists and their methods
objectives: Use list methods like append, remove, pop

teachingContent.beginner: Lists are ordered collections that can store multiple items. You can add, remove, and access items easily.
teachingContent.intermediate: Lists are mutable sequences. They support indexing, slicing, and have many built-in methods.
teachingContent.advanced: Understanding list comprehensions, memory management, and when to use lists vs tuples vs sets.

crossQuestions: How do you add an item to a list?
What's the difference between append and extend?
How do you access the last item in a list?

concepts.title: Functions and Parameters
concepts.description: Learn how to define and use functions in Python

teachingContent.beginner: Functions are reusable blocks of code. You define them with 'def' and call them by name.
teachingContent.intermediate: Functions can have positional arguments, keyword arguments, default values, and *args/**kwargs.
teachingContent.advanced: Understanding function scope, closures, decorators, and first-class functions.

crossQuestions: How do you define a function in Python?
What's the purpose of the return statement?
How do you set a default value for a parameter?

concepts.title: Dictionaries
concepts.description: Learn about Python dictionaries and their methods

teachingContent.beginner: Dictionaries store data in key-value pairs. You use keys to access values, like a real dictionary uses words to find definitions.
teachingContent.intermediate: Dictionaries are mutable, unordered collections. They provide O(1) lookup time for keys.
teachingContent.advanced: Understanding dictionary comprehensions, OrderedDict, defaultdict, and when to use dictionaries vs other data structures.

crossQuestions: How do you create a dictionary?
How do you access a value using a key?
What happens if you try to access a key that doesn't exist?

concepts.title: Loops - For and While

teachingContent.beginner: Loops let you repeat code multiple times. 'for' loops iterate over sequences, 'while' loops run until a condition is false.
teachingContent.intermediate: Python's for loop works with any iterable. Use enumerate() for index-value pairs, zip() for parallel iteration.
teachingContent.advanced: Understanding iterators, generators, and the iteration protocol. When to use list comprehensions vs loops.

crossQuestions: Write a for loop that prints numbers 1 to 5
What's the difference between for and while loops?
